rounds.title: Final Interview Gauntlet
rounds.description: A timed mixed hiring loop covering SQL, statistics, analytics case structure and behavioral communication.

questions.context: The hiring panel gives you the cross-company capstone KPI table and asks for current exception rates.
questions.prompt: Using capstone_company_kpis, return company_key and exception_rate for Current rows ordered by exception_rate descending.
questions.explanation: A strong SQL answer filters to the requested period and returns the exact company-level metric in descending order.

questions.context: Two business units improved service score after spending more, while three had smaller cost changes.
options: The pattern can motivate further analysis, but it does not prove additional cost caused service improvement because business mix and other operational changes may confound the comparison.
The higher cost definitely caused the service improvement.
Correlation and causation are the same when the sample contains five companies.
The two higher-cost companies should be removed as outliers before interpretation.
questions.expectedAnswer: The pattern can motivate further analysis, but it does not prove additional cost caused service improvement because business mix and other operational changes may confound the comparison.
questions.explanation: Interview-ready analysis separates observed association from causal claims and calls out plausible confounding.

questions.context: A product leader asks why a KPI fell 8% this month and wants a recommendation by tomorrow.
questions.prompt: Describe the analysis structure you would use before making a recommendation.

criteria.label: Confirm metric definition and data quality

questions.explanation: A strong case answer starts with definition and data quality, then segments, compares, tests hypotheses and ends with a bounded action.

questions.context: A manager asks you to change a dashboard number because it looks bad before an executive review.
questions.explanation: A professional analyst protects metric integrity while clarifying the business concern and offering transparent context instead of manipulating the number.

questions.context: The panel wants to compare baseline and current service scores across five businesses.
options: Grouped bar or dumbbell chart showing baseline and current score side by side for each company
A 3D pie chart with every period as a slice
questions.expectedAnswer: Grouped bar or dumbbell chart showing baseline and current score side by side for each company
questions.explanation: A paired comparison chart makes direction and magnitude visible without hiding company-level variation.

questions.context: You have 60 seconds with an executive who asks what to do with mixed service, cost and exception-rate results.
questions.prompt: Write the structure of your executive answer.
questions.explanation: Executive communication should move from finding to evidence, limitation, action and monitoring.
